run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-15T08:33:39Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend is explained by the ad service being unavailable: the workload's only pod (ad-554b849958-l9ft5, deployment ad with spec.replicas=1) was OOMKilled repeatedly (exitCode 137, restartCount 4) and went into CrashLoopBackOff, so the ad Service ended up with no ready endpoints. Frontend's gRPC client spans for oteldemo.AdService/GetAds and its /api/data route failed at ~100% during the incident (0.9/s ERROR versus 0/s UNSET at 08:40:39), with error spans also on the upstream tcp.connect operation, and the same failures surface at frontend-proxy as error spans on its ingress and router frontend egress operations. Frontend's other operations, its pod health and its resources were normal, so the failure is isolated to the ad dependency path. The exact alert expression could not be validated because no alerting rules are present in this Prometheus, and no spans were retained for the incident window, so the causal parent-child edge is inferred from matching timing and operation names rather than from a trace.

claims.text: At the alert start 2026-11-15T08:33:39Z, frontend's error spans were confined to the ad path: span_name grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds STATUS_CODE_ERROR 0.1222/s, GET /api/data 0.1222/s, executing api route (pages) /api/data 0.1222/s, GET 0.1222/s and tcp.connect 0.0333/s; every other frontend operation (CartService/AddItem, CartService/GetCart, CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, ProductCatalogService/GetProduct, RecommendationService/ListRecommendations, /api/cart, /api/checkout, /api/products/[productId], /api/recommendations, render route (pages) /, resolve page components, POST) had STATUS_CODE_ERROR at 0.
Frontend's aggregate error-span rate began rising in the minute 08:32:00-08:33:00 (1m rate 0 before, 4.7/s at the 08:33:00 evaluation), peaked at 9.27/s at 08:40:00 and was still 5.67/s at 08:42:00.

At 08:40:39 frontend's grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds client spans were 0.9/s STATUS_CODE_ERROR and 0/s STATUS_CODE_UNSET, and its GET /api/data and executing api route (pages) /api/data spans were likewise 0.9/s ERROR and 0/s UNSET, while frontend GET overall was 7.11/s UNSET plus 0.9/s ERROR. Across 08:38-08:42 the GetAds and /api/data error rate held at 1.06-1.12/s with 0 successes, i.e. those ad-dependent operations were failing entirely.

The ad workload's only pod, ad-554b849958-l9ft5 (deployment ad, spec.replicas 1, created 2026-11-15T07:55:15Z), has restartCount 4 and kubelet recorded reason OOMKilled with exitCode 137 for the previous container instance (startedAt 08:34:23Z, finishedAt 08:34:53Z) and for the current instance (startedAt 08:35:44Z, finishedAt 08:35:55Z); the ad container is not ready and the pod's Ready condition has been False (ContainersNotReady) since 08:35:56Z, with node-level unavailableReplicas 1 on deployment ad.

Events for ad-554b849958-l9ft5 in the window include Normal Created/Started container ad with count 6 (last 08:37:24Z) and Warning BackOff count 23 (last 08:40:32Z) with message 'Back-off restarting failed container ad in pod ad-554b849958-l9ft5_otel-demo'.

The ad container runs with memory limit 450Mi / request 225Mi and CPU limit 50m; its working set grew monotonically from 331,444,224 bytes at the 08:08 point to 371,867,648 bytes at the 08:35 point for the long-lived container instance before the OOM kills.
The ad Service currently has zero ready endpoints: its endpoint subset lists only notReadyAddresses 100.96.2.230 on port 8080 with no ready addresses, matching selector opentelemetry.io/name=ad.

Ad service span activity collapsed during the same period: total ad span rate fell from 2.19/s at 08:25 to 1.89/s at 08:33, 1.03/s at 08:35, 0.14/s at 08:37 and 0/s from 08:39 onward, with STATUS_CODE_ERROR at 0/s throughout, while frontend total span rate stayed near 55/s.

frontend-proxy shows its own error spans in the same window and with the same onset: at 08:40:39 span_name ingress had 0.9/s ERROR versus 9.01/s UNSET and span_name router frontend egress had 0.893/s ERROR versus 9.02/s UNSET; its error-rate timeline rises at the 08:33 point together with frontend's (0.259/s at 08:33, 1.96/s at 08:37, 2.24/s at 08:40).

Per-service STATUS_CODE_ERROR rates at 08:40:39 were frontend 3.61/s and frontend-proxy 1.79/s, with recommendation 0.0037/s and fraud-detection, accounting, payment and ad at 0/s; the 5-minute increase of frontend error spans at 08:40:00 was 1300 spans.

Both the ad and frontend ReplicaSets and their pods were created at 2026-11-15T07:55:15Z, i.e. about 37 minutes before the error onset, with images ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad and ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-frontend; the ad ReplicaSet is ad-554b849958 and the frontend ReplicaSet is frontend-675fd7b5c5.

Ad container log lines available for 2026-11-15T08:28:00-08:45:00 were 416; the 120 shown lines (08:30:37-08:31:44) contain only normal request handling ('Targeted ad request received for [...]', 'Non-targeted ad request received, preparing random response.', 'no baggage found in context') with no error or OOM text.

Frontend itself was not resource-starved or restarting: pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-jfvbx is Running with container ready=true and restartCount 0, its working set stayed flat at about 128-129 MB against a 200Mi limit across 08:25-08:47, and its CPU throttling rate was essentially unchanged before and during the incident (4.45-5.35 throttled periods/s from 08:25 to 08:42), so frontend-side saturation does not explain the error burst.

Hypothesis that the alert reflects a general network or multi-dependency failure is rejected: at 08:33:39 frontend's client spans for CartService/AddItem, CartService/GetCart, CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, ProductCatalogService/GetProduct and RecommendationService/ListRecommendations all had STATUS_CODE_ERROR 0, and its /api/cart and /api/checkout routes had 0 error spans, so only the ad call path failed.

Hypothesis that ad's restarts were a planned rollout or rescheduling is rejected: the crash terminations carry reason OOMKilled with exitCode 137, kubelet emitted 23 Warning BackOff events for the same pod, the owning ReplicaSet ad-554b849958 and the pod were created at 07:55:15Z and no replacement pod name appeared, so this is a crash loop rather than a controller replacement.

Hypothesis that a traffic surge drove the ad OOM is not supported: ad's own span rate declined from 2.19/s at 08:25 to 1.89/s at the 08:33 point and frontend's total span rate stayed near 55/s (54.6-57.3/s across 08:25-08:37), so no load increase preceded the memory exhaustion and crashes.

Most likely causal chain: the ad pod exceeded its 450Mi memory limit and was OOMKilled repeatedly, leaving the ad Service without ready endpoints, so frontend's GetAds calls failed entirely and produced the error spans on grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, GET /api/data and executing api route (pages) /api/data that raised the RequestErrorRate alert for frontend. The timing matches (frontend errors start in 08:32-08:33, ad container memory growing through the 08:30s, OOMKilled at 08:34:53 and 08:35:55, BackOff until after 08:40), but because no spans exist for the incident window the dependency edge is inferred from operation names and timing, not from a trace.

The memory pressure inside the ad container looks like gradual unbounded growth rather than a burst: its working set rose monotonically from about 331 MB to about 372 MB between the 08:08 and 08:35 points while request volume was flat or declining, and the container was then killed by the kernel with reason OOMKilled. Whether this is an application leak in image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad or simply a limit (450Mi) too small for its steady state cannot be separated with the evidence available.

frontend-proxy's error spans on ingress and router frontend egress are the upstream manifestation of the same frontend failures: its error onset coincides with frontend's and its ERROR rate (about 0.9/s ingress, 0.89/s router frontend egress at 08:40:39) matches frontend's /api/data error rate, but the parent-child edge is not visible because no trace covers the window.

Raise or profile the ad container's memory budget (currently limit 450Mi / request 225Mi on image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad) and determine why its working set grows monotonically; the deployment also has spec.replicas 1 and the container has no readinessProbe, so a single crashing pod removes all ad capacity and readiness is inferred from process liveness only.

Consider running the ad workload with more than one replica and a readiness probe so that a single OOM-killed pod does not make the whole ad Service endpoint-less, and add pod memory-usage alerting ahead of the container limit so growth is visible before OOMKills start.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate alerting rule is not present in this Prometheus: list_prometheus_rules returned no_data both for rule_name RequestErrorRate and for type=alert, so the alert's exact expression, window and aggregation are unknown, and the reported current value 2.622222222222222 could not be reproduced from the available metrics (observed frontend STATUS_CODE_ERROR span rates were 0.52/s over 5m at 08:33:39, rising to roughly 3.6-4.5/s around 08:38-08:42).

No Jaeger spans were available inside the incident window: traces_search and traces_search_by_tags for frontend in 08:28-08:45 returned no traces, so span-level error messages, the exact gRPC status returned to frontend, and the parent-child edge from the /api/data route to the GetAds client span could not be verified. The one large frontend trace result that was returned (RESULT_TOO_LARGE, status error) was reported with source_end_at around 08:23:55, i.e. before the error onset, so trace detail for the failure window is missing.

Ad container application logs for the crash period are missing: an unfiltered log query for ad-554b849958-l9ft5 over 08:32:00-08:40:00 returned zero lines, and the previous container instance's log stream was reported unavailable (previous terminated container 'ad' not found), so no app-side error, panic or memory-limit message from before the OOM kill was readable.

change_history is not an integrated source in this Run, so no change record explains why ad memory grew or whether the ad image/limits changed: the only change signal observed is that the ad and frontend ReplicaSets and pods were created at 07:55:15Z with images 2.1.3-ad and 2.1.3-frontend, and the previous image/version and any config change before it could not be verified.

kube-state-metrics series for workload availability (kube_deployment_status_replicas_available / _ready, kube_replicaset_owner, kube_pod_owner) are absent from this Prometheus, so only the current deployment/pod objects could be inspected; ad's replicas-available history during the window is unknown.

Trace-derived metric values were not stable between successive evaluations (for example the same 08:40:39 instant returned 0.9/s versus 1.08/s for the GetAds error rate, and the summed rate was 3.61/s while the per-operation sum was 2.72/s), so exact error totals and any precise percentage should be treated as approximate; the trace-metric data also ends around 08:45-08:46, so whether the incident had ended by 08:51 is unknown and the declining tail of the rate series may be a data-edge artifact rather than recovery.

Currency's STATUS_CODE_ERROR series was not returned by the per-service error query at 08:33:39 (only accounting 'orders receive' at 0), so currency's error state is unknown rather than zero; the own health of cart, checkout, product-catalog, currency, email, shipping, quote and image-provider was not evaluated beyond frontend's call paths to them and the per-service error series that were returned.

The exact moment the ad container first became unavailable is only bounded to roughly 08:32-08:33 (frontend error onset) because no container start/finish records exist for the two earlier restarts of the four reported restarts.
next_steps: Read the ad pod's earlier container terminations from the container runtime or kubelet logs to confirm all four restarts were OOMKilled, and capture a memory profile of image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad to distinguish a leak from an undersized 450Mi limit.
Retrieve the RequestErrorRate rule definition from the Alertmanager/Prometheus rule source to confirm its PromQL expression, window and the meaning of the reported value 2.622222222222222.
Check deployment history (helm/CI) for otel-demo around 2026-11-15T07:55:15Z to see whether the 2.1.3-ad image or its resource limits were introduced then.
After any ad container restart, verify frontend's GetAds and /api/data error spans return to zero and that the ad Service regains ready endpoints before treating the alert as resolved.
